open_points.subject: authorization refusal result versus K-17 refusal-code rule
open_points.text: “whose failure is `not_permitted` and is distinct from an operation's own `refused` result” conflicts with K-17: “A refusal carries a distinct code only where some caller acts on the difference; otherwise one refusal with a reason for the trace.” No caller behavior based on this distinction is stated.
open_points.question: Which caller acts differently on `not_permitted` and `refused`, or should these results not have distinct codes?
options: Name the caller and the behavior that depends on the distinction
Use one refusal code and retain the distinction only as a reason
Amend K-17 so this distinction does not require a caller that acts on it
open_points.default_guess: Keep the newly explicit `not_permitted` result and amend K-17 to allow the authorization-versus-operation distinction.
